subject: Social Science
central_question: How do historians measure historical time using calendars and timelines, gather evidence from many different sources, and use that evidence to understand how early humans lived?
in_scope_units: How Do We Learn About the Past?: Earth's very long history and the four kinds of experts
How Is Time Measured in History?: eras, calendars, AD/BC to CE/BCE shift, timelines
Calculating and naming spans of time: BCE-to-CE calculation, century, millennium, panchanga
What Are the Sources of History?: literary, archaeological, oral and artistic sources
The Beginnings of Human History: early Homo sapiens, hunter-gatherers, tools, rock paintings
The First Crops: Ice Age, shift to farming, domesticating animals, social complexity
banned_topics: Detailed features of the Indus-Sarasvati/Harappan civilisation (covered in Chapter 6)
The ancient and foreign names of India, such as Bharata or Hindustan (covered in Chapter 5)

known_pitfalls.claim: The Gregorian calendar has a year zero, so counting years from BCE to CE is simple subtraction.
known_pitfalls.correction: There is no 'year zero'; year 1 CE follows immediately after year 1 BCE, so add the BCE and CE year numbers and subtract 1.

known_pitfalls.claim: AD/BC and CE/BCE refer to two entirely different dating systems.
known_pitfalls.correction: CE and BCE are simply the terms now used worldwide for the same points in time that used to be marked AD and BC.

known_pitfalls.claim: History is studied only from written texts.
known_pitfalls.correction: Sources beyond text include archaeological, oral and artistic sources, plus scientific studies like genetics and climate studies.

known_pitfalls.claim: Early humans lived alone or in isolated single families.
known_pitfalls.correction: Early humans lived in bands or groups to help each other.

known_pitfalls.claim: The shift from hunting-gathering to farming happened everywhere at exactly the same time and pace.
known_pitfalls.correction: This happened gradually, in many parts of the world, after the last Ice Age ended around 12,000 years ago.
